$comment: The fifth review of the interpolation judgement, judged by both editors alike: a literal Trusted counts toward a URL that loads code with its own text, as interpolate judges it; a name declared Trusted or set to Trusted(...) is Trusted; a call to toLong() and its kind is a number; a call that changes a declared String is a String.

cases.name: a Trusted origin before a value fixes the host of a URL that loads code
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s%s\"></script>", Trusted("https://cdn.example.com/"), q)

cases.name: a Trusted path before a value fixes the host of a URL that loads code
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s%s\"></script>", Trusted("/js/"), q)

cases.name: an empty Trusted before a value fixes nothing, and interpolate always throws on the value
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s%s\"></script>", Trusted(""), q)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: q lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Only Trusted(...) is let in there. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a Trusted whose text is not known before a value may fix the host
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(p: String, q: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s%s\"></script>", Trusted(p), q)

issues.message: interpolate throws here unless the Trusted text before q fixes the host or q is Trusted(...): it lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a value before a Trusted is the one named
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s%s\"></script>", q, Trusted("/js/a.js"))

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: q lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Only Trusted(...) is let in there. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a top-level val set to Trusted is Trusted
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
val CDN = Trusted("https://cdn.example.com/x.js")
fun f() = interpolate("<script src=\"%s\"></script>", CDN)

cases.name: a Trusted in a Kotlin template in the format is markup, read as format

issues.message: Kotlin fills in $t before interpolate reads the markup, so interpolate reads what it holds as markup too: a %s in it is a hole and a %% a per cent sign, and interpolate throws or changes the markup. Make it a %s hole and pass the Html: interpolate writes an Html or a Trusted there as it is.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.* fun f(t: Trusted) = interpolate("

%s %s

", t, 1)

cases.name: a val set to Trusted in a Kotlin template in the format is markup

issues.message: Kotlin fills in $t before interpolate reads the markup, so interpolate reads what it holds as markup too: a %s in it is a hole and a %% a per cent sign, and interpolate throws or changes the markup. Make it a %s hole and pass the Html: interpolate writes an Html or a Trusted there as it is.

cases.name: a sum converted with toInt() is a number
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.* fun f(a: UInt, b: UInt) = interpolate("""

""", (a + b).toInt())

cases.name: a safe call to toLong() may be null
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.* fun f(u: UInt?) = interpolate("""

""", u?.toLong())

issues.message: interpolate throws here unless u?.toLong() is a number or a boolean: it lands in data-signals, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Put the value in a signal and reference it from the expression, or write the signal's name in the markup yourself.

cases.name: a sum that ends in toInt() is not known to be a number
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.* fun f(s: String, u: UInt) = interpolate("""

""", s + u.toInt())

issues.message: interpolate throws here unless s + u.toInt() is a number: it lands in style, which is read as CSS. Pass a number and write the unit in the markup, or choose between classes.

cases.name: trim of a declared String is a String

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${query.trim()} into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(query: String) = interpolate("

x

", query.trim()).text

cases.name: take, replace and a chain of them on a declared String are a String

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${query.take(3)} into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it.

Kotlin writes ${query.replace("a", "b").lower…} into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).

cases.name: ifBlank with a String on a declared String is a String

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${query.ifBlank { "none" }} into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).
